test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 29 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Due to the need for irrigation facilities and pesticides/fertilisers, the first phase of the Green Revolution benefitted few affluent states such as _____________.

options.text: Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh

solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first phase of the Green Revolution in India (1960s-70s) focused on improving agricultural productivity through **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, irrigation, and chemical fertilizers.**
 
• States like **Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu** benefitted the most due to better access to irrigation facilities and agricultural infrastructure.
 
• **Punjab** emerged as the leader in wheat production, while **Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu** excelled in rice production during this period.
 
• The revolution primarily favored regions with well-established irrigation systems, leaving rain-fed and economically weaker states behind.
 
• This phase contributed significantly to India’s food security but also led to economic disparities between regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• An agricultural reform initiative in the 1960s aimed at increasing food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, using modern techniques.
 
• Introduced by Dr. Norman Borlaug globally and spearheaded in India by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan.
 
• Key components included high-yield variety seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Punjab:**
 
 
• Punjab became the "Granary of India" due to the adoption of Green Revolution techniques.
 
• Widespread use of tube wells and canals boosted irrigation, leading to a sharp rise in wheat production.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Over-dependence on chemical fertilizers led to soil degradation.
 
• Water-intensive crops like rice caused groundwater depletion in states like Punjab and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Uneven benefits created regional and class-based disparities in agricultural development.
 
 
 
• **Second Phase of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• Launched in the 1980s to address regional imbalances by focusing on eastern and rain-fed states like Bihar, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• Emphasized sustainable agricultural practices, including diversification and water management.
